annotations.text:
Court, taken further: the app lives on one court at dusk.

Deep glass blue for their half, turf green for ours, warm floodlight spilling in from one corner, and the ball as the only bright thing on screen. Nothing here is a system list or a system button — full-bleed color, soft 20-24px shapes, hand-drawn icons.

The net is drawn as it looks from directly above: a bright tape line with a post at each end, not a band of mesh. Every screen split into two halves carries it, score screens included.

The boards are set in Unbounded and Golos Text; the app is not. Both faces were declined (ADR-0006) and every size goes through the ramp in PadelDesign — the board decides which ramp entry a thing gets, not how many points it is.

The four boards for screens that have shipped were deleted: the screen is the design once it exists. These two are what phone-scoring tickets 06 and 07 build.

The ball is the app's one character. It waits on the net before the match, sits in the serving half's corner during play, and rides the New match button. It is the same object every time you see it — that is where the soul is meant to come from, not from decoration.

One colour only. The light is warm white — light, not a hue — and the ball's yellow is the single colour in the app. It marks what is yours and what is chosen: your serve, your half, your start button. Losses go cold and grey. Nothing needs a red, and nothing needs a second accent to argue with.
